{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZer3SA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDF5kg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 65, "title": "Implement V30 memory-operand ROL4/ROR4 nibble rotations", "body": "## Problem

The VM profile cannot execute the documented V30 memory-operand nibble rotations `ROL4` and `ROR4`. Its [NEC opcode dispatcher](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1/src/cpu.rs#L1741) accepts only extensions `10h–1Fh`; `0F 28` and `0F 2A` stop with an unsupported-opcode diagnostic.

Implementing these memory forms adds missing CPU behavior using the existing effective-address and Bus access paths. This Issue covers one independently testable part of V30 support.

## Expected outcome

On `Pc9801Vm`, implement `ROL4 mem8` (`0F 28 /0`) and `ROR4 mem8` (`0F 2A /0`), with memory ModR/M forms only. There is no immediate operand. For pre-instruction memory byte `d` and accumulator nibble `a = AL & 0Fh`:

| Instruction | New memory byte | New AL low nibble |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ROL4 | `((d << 4) & F0h) \| a` | `d >> 4` |
| ROR4 | `(a << 4) \| (d >> 4)` | `d & 0Fh` |

Flags are unaffected. NEC leaves AL’s upper nibble unspecified; preserve it as a deterministic emulator policy and identify that policy separately from hardware guarantees. AH and other registers remain unchanged. These semantics and encodings follow [NEC’s V-series Instruction Manual, printed pp.136 and 141](https://www.ardent-tool.com/CPU/docs/NEC/V20-V30/v_series.pdf#page=147).

Use the existing 16-bit addressing, segment selection and Bus mapping. Snapshot the inputs before updating either output. Access exactly one destination byte.

Scope excludes register destinations, including AL overlap, other NEC extensions, new LOCK/REP behavior, Ap opcode implementation and cycle accuracy. Retain explicit unsupported diagnostics for excluded encodings without presenting them as hardware exception behavior.

## Context and reproduction

Inspected baseline: `e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1`. No files were changed and no builds, tests or fixture preparation were executed by this evaluator. Supplied open Issues are empty; the supplied completed history contains no nibble-rotation implementation.

Minimal original reproduction for the Coordinator:

1. Initialize VM CPU execution in conventional RAM with `DS=0`, `[2000h]=12h`, `AL=83h`, a nonzero AH and saved FLAGS.
2. Execute `0F 28 06 00 20`.
3. Current behavior: unsupported V30 opcode diagnostic. Expected memory: `23h`; AL low nibble: `1`. Under the preservation policy, AL is `81h`.
4. Repeat from the initial state with `0F 2A 06 00 20`. Expected memory: `31h`; AL low nibble: `2`; policy AL: `82h`.

NEC documents these memory transformations using initial memory `12h` and accumulator nibble `3`, and states that neither instruction changes flags: [V20/V30 User’s Manual, Section 12, printed pp.12-45–12-46](https://www.dosdays.co.uk/media/nec/NEC-V20-V30-Users-Manual.pdf).

Existing [V30 bit-operation tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1/tests/core.rs#L173), [original carry-repeat guest acceptance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1/tests/core.rs#L1342), and its [provenance manifest](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1/fixtures/v30-repc-manifest.json) provide relevant conventions.

Project progress: merged PR #64 adds PIC polling and cascade propagation. The Coordinator reports 263 native integration tests and 96 production release-Wasm browser tests passing; the browser run changed server ports after a startup conflict. [The repository validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e43f21084f366120dc0d5951bd8b64ae837ddaa1/docs/validation.md#issue-63-8259a-ocw3-polling-2026-10-24) supports that attribution. Independent review and remote CI results were not supplied. PIC remains partial.

Retain all inventory scopes and statuses:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio, integration |
| implemented_unverified | ide, grcg |
| unimplemented | paging, fpu |

After this Issue, V30 still requires register-operand nibble rotations, packed-BCD string operations, bit-field extensions, TF traps, NMI and broader instruction/prefix/fault acceptance. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 retain their fixed required scope. No category becomes verified through this bounded change.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add and record the minimal Rust reproduction failing before production changes and passing afterward. Check both instructions, exact instruction advancement, unchanged FLAGS/AH, destination byte and accumulator result.
- [ ] Add focused native tests covering all 256 destination values and all 16 incoming accumulator nibbles for both directions. Include nondecimal nibbles and different incoming AL upper nibbles. Derive expected results independently from the documented nibble mapping. Distinguish tests of the upper-nibble preservation policy from hardware-defined results.
- [ ] Cover every 16-bit effective-address family, direct addressing, signed disp8, disp16, BP-default SS, other default DS addressing, and ES/CS/SS/DS overrides using distinct segments. Include effective-address wrapping, offset `FFFFh`, and VM 20-bit physical wrapping. Assert neighbor guards, unchanged unrelated registers, complete flag preservation and forward progress.
- [ ] Demonstrate that accesses use the Bus: cover a write-protected ROM destination and a planar VRAM destination with GRCG disabled, preserving existing mapping behavior. For representative RAM cases, check that no bytes outside the destination change.
- [ ] Keep register destinations and nonzero ModR/M.reg encodings explicitly unsupported for this Issue, without operand/register writes. Add Ap negative coverage proving these bytes do not execute NEC rotations; preserve its existing diagnostic behavior without claiming that diagnostic is an i486 hardware exception.
- [ ] Add an original MIT assembly probe, for example `guest/v30_nibble_mem.asm`, with offline preparation and a checked manifest. Record source/license, assembly command, source/boot/image SHA-256 hashes, result layout, exact expected bytes, guards and execution budget. Store masked accumulator results when asserting hardware-defined behavior. Generated media remains outside the publication tree. Introduce no commercial media, proprietary ROMs or copied emulator implementation.
- [ ] Native and production release-Wasm browser tests boot the same VM probe before and after reset; browsers cover `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require guest-produced PASS only after checking both rotations, flags and guards; exact host-checked results; unchanged disk bytes; no FAIL/core/browser errors; and completion within 2,000,000 slots per boot. Hosts may insert, reset, step and read, but must not patch results or emulate the tested instructions.
- [ ] Integrate offline probe preparation into acceptance CI and document its reproducible command. Suggested focused commands are `cargo test --locked --test core v30_nibble_mem_` and `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 ap_v30_nibble_mem_`.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the applicable README fixture prerequisites, focused tests, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`, including the production Wasm/publication checks and both browser roots. Preserve existing hardware, CPU-shadow, DOS/application, VM and six-game assertions and budgets. Report exact outcomes and any port-only browser configuration adjustment.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility documentation with the implemented operand subset, specification links, deterministic policy, actual validation and remaining V30 work. Review the final diff against this Issue before merge. Limited probes or existing game results must not be described as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
